problems.title: Greedy or not?
problems.statement: Which are solved correctly by an obvious greedy?

options: Maximum non-overlapping intervals by earliest end

problems.solution: {1, 3, 4} makes 6 as 4 + 1 + 1 greedily, versus 3 + 3. Density greedy fails 0/1 knapsack (it works for fractional knapsack).

problems.title: Jumps
hints: Layer 0: {0}; layer 1: indices 1–3; layer 2: up to 6; …
problems.solution: Layers end at 0, 3, 6 and 7, so 3 jumps (for example 0 → 2 → 5 → 7).

problems.title: Gas station
problems.solution: The tank goes negative at index 1, so restart at 2: 3, 1, 2, then wrap: 3, 1 ≥ 0. Start 2.

problems.title: Proof styles
problems.solution: Reach after d jumps; swapping the first interval; a lower bound matched by a schedule.

problems.title: Candy
hints: Left pass, right pass, take the max.

problems.title: Elimination
problems.statement: In gas station, starting at s you run dry before reaching j + 1.

parts.prompt: Which starts can you rule out?

hints: You arrived at each with tank ≥ 0.
problems.solution: Starting later, with an empty tank, is no better than arriving there with a non-negative tank, so the whole range fails.

problems.title: Verify a greedy
problems.statement: In an online assessment your greedy passes the samples but you can't prove it.

options: Write a brute force and compare on random small inputs

problems.solution: A brute-force check on thousands of tiny cases finds most greedy counterexamples in seconds.

problems.title: Largest number

options: a before b iff a + b > b + a (as strings)

problems.solution: "330" > "303", so 3 comes before 30: 9 5 34 3 30 → 9534330. The comparator is transitive, which is what makes the sort valid.
